summary: John Henry Wright was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College and Leipzig University under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard University (~1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.

John Herbert Harington worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of the Asiatic Society, and as an honorary professor at Fort William College (~1801–1823).

John Hick worked in philosophy and religious studies, having studied at Scarborough College, the University of Edinburgh, and Oriel College, Oxford. His career included posts at Cornell, Princeton Theological Seminary, Cambridge, the University of Birmingham (~1967–1982), and Claremont Graduate University (~1982–1992).

John Hurrell Crook studied at Southampton, Cambridge, and under Sheng Yen, working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at the University of Bristol (~1963–1989), held a fellowship at CASBS (~1968–1969), and was affiliated with the Université Bouddhique Européenne.

John J. Holder is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006–2018).

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and several traditional teachers. He held posts at Boston College, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

John James Jones was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Aberystwyth University (~1912–1916). He served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales from around 1926 to 1957.

John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After completing his MA at the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner, he held academic posts at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

John Kieschnick is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Bristol from around 2005 to 2011 before becoming a professor of Buddhist studies at Stanford University in 2011.

John Lane Bell is a philosopher who studied at Oxford (~1963–1969). He held positions at the London School of Economics (~1969–1989), the National University of Singapore, and the University of Western Ontario (~1989–2021).

John Leyden was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Edinburgh and under Henry Thomas Colebrooke. He served at the Asiatic Society (~1806–1811) and was a professor of Hindustani at Fort William College in 1808.

John Lockwood Kipling was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875), served as Principal of the National College of Arts, and was Curator of the Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles A. Moore, and George T. Artola, and served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

John M. Rosenfield worked in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Berkeley, SMU, Iowa, and Harvard under Benjamin Rowland, he taught at Iowa, UCLA, and Harvard (1965–1991), where he also curated at the Harvard Art Museums.

John Marshall was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Cambridge, the British School at Athens, and under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.

John Muir was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow, East India Company College, and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and at the University of Edinburgh.
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lopon Tenzin Namdak, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Namkhai Norbu.

John Nemec is an Indologist who studied at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and Penn. He serves as Associate Professor of Indian Religions and South Asian Studies at the University of Virginia.

John Okell was a linguist who studied at the University of Oxford and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London from 1959 to 1999.

John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota and with Noriaki Hakamaya, later serving at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture and Middlebury College.
